claims.claim: On Christmas Eve a group round the fire tells ghost stories
claims.evidence: 'The story had held us, round the fire... on Christmas Eve in an old house, a strange tale should essentially be'

claims.claim: Douglas offers a manuscript about two children and sends for it
claims.evidence: 'I shall have to send to town... The story's written. It's in a locked drawer'; 'a small nephew and a small niece'

claims.claim: The account was written years ago by a young governess hired by a man in Harley Street and sent to his country house
claims.evidence: 'it has not been out for years'; 'a house in Harley Street'; 'his country home, an old family place in Essex'
searched the text; she is only 'the governess' / 'my friend' in the frame, never given a name

claims.claim: Miles and Flora at Bly, an Essex country house
claims.evidence: 'an old family place in Essex'; Bly named in the text

claims.claim: Their uncle tells her never to trouble him
claims.evidence: 'That she should never trouble him—but never, never'

claims.claim: Miles has been dismissed from school
She sees Peter Quint, a dead valet, and Miss Jessel, the dead former governess
claims.evidence: 'Peter Quint—his own man, his valet'; 'He died.'; Miss Jessel discussed as the earlier governess who has died

claims.claim: Mrs. Grose is the housekeeper and helps protect the children
claims.evidence: 'housekeeper and was also acting for the time as superintendent'

claims.claim: Flora falls ill and Mrs. Grose takes her away
claims.evidence: 'Flora was so markedly feverish'; governess to Mrs. Grose: 'It's you who must go. You must take [Flora]'

claims.claim: Alone with Miles, the governess makes him name Quint, and he dies in her arms
claims.evidence: 'Peter Quint—you devil!'; 'his little heart, dispossessed, had stopped'
'he began to read to our hushed little circle on the night of the fourth'
